headline_assumptions.note: Assumption: cardlock fleet fueling site discount versus the EIA average, dollars per gallon; in line with typical advertised fleet fuel-card network discounts (network averages of about 12 and 15 cents; 10 to 25 cents at major truck stops). Owner's figures from the networks' own advertising; no source is cited here because naming the networks would break the project's no-company-names rule
Assumption: synthetic drivers only fuel where truck access is confirmed

Assumption: bulk diesel delivered to the Phoenix DC tank costs this much less than the EIA weekly retail average, dollars per gallon; within a vendor-quoted bulk range of 15 to 30 cents (owner's figure; no public source)
Assumption: share of linehaul departures that leave without the yard fill (tank queue, late load); a skipped truck uses the card only if it runs low mid-trip
Assumption: daily Phoenix DC to Tucson yard round trips, one tractor each; the sixth linehaul tractor is a spare
synthetic-route assumption: openrouteservice road miles over the synthetic route plans

headline_assumptions.value: Named truck stops on I-10 between Casa Grande and Eloy (truck access confirmed)
headline_assumptions.note: Assumption: the hypothetical fuel partner program is the named, truck-confirmed truck stops on the I-10 stretch from Casa Grande to Eloy (replaces a random draw)

Assumption: partner discount off the posted price, cents per gallon; in line with typical advertised fleet fuel-card network discounts (network averages of about 12 and 15 cents; 10 to 25 cents at major truck stops). Owner's figures from the networks' own advertising; no source is cited here because naming the networks would break the project's no-company-names rule
Assumption: stations farther than this from a route are never a sensible detour; kept equal to fueling.search_radius_mi so every station a driver could pick has detour figures

Fact (averaged by us): Tucson Travel Time Index, mean of the four FHWA Urban Congestion Report quarters Oct 2025 to Sep 2026 (1.09, 1.09, 1.04, 1.05), freeways; https://ops.fhwa.dot.gov/perf_measurement/ucr/reports/fy2026_q4.pdf
Fact (averaged by us): Tucson Planning Time Index (95th percentile, late one day a month), mean of the same four FHWA quarters (1.55, 1.39, 1.31, 1.28); same source
Setting: when true, peak detour minutes use the Planning Time Index instead of the Travel Time Index (the conservative, plan-for-a-bad-day view)
Fact: FHWA Urban Congestion Report peak periods (weekday AM 6 to 9, PM 4 to 7); https://ops.fhwa.dot.gov/perf_measurement/ucr/documentation.htm
Assumption: a detour longer than this (after the time-of-day factor) is never recommended or counted
Assumption: cost of each detour minute taken before the route's last customer delivery, for the risk of a late delivery

Fact: FMCSA hours of service, property-carrying drivers may drive a total of 11 hours (49 CFR 395.3(a)(3)(i)); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/subtitle-B/chapter-III/subchapter-B/part-395/subpart-A/section-395.3

Fact: FMCSA hours of service, no driving after 14 consecutive hours on duty (49 CFR 395.3(a)(2)); the short-haul exception (150 air-miles, 49 CFR 395.1(e)(1)) keeps the 14-hour limit; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/subtitle-B/chapter-III/subchapter-B/part-395/subpart-A/section-395.1

Assumption: loaded cost, wage plus benefits for a foodservice route driver, dollars per hour. Basis: BLS OEWS, Heavy and Tractor-Trailer Truck Drivers (53-3032): national median $57,440 a year (May 2024); Tucson metro median $27.23 an hour (May 2025, the latest Tucson figure, BLS series OEUM004606000000053303208); foodservice routes pay above the metro median; https://www.bls.gov/ooh/transportation-and-material-moving/heavy-and-tractor-trailer-truck-drivers.htm and https://data.bls.gov/timeseries/OEUM004606000000053303208

Assumption: stop-and-go miles per gallon on city delivery routes. Source: NACFE, Run on Less Regional (2019), Class 8 regional haul average estimated at 6.0 MPG; https://nacfe.org/research/run-on-less/run-on-less-regional/

Assumption: highway miles per gallon for a loaded tractor-trailer. Basis: ATRI, An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking, 2026 Update, reports 6.73 mpg at 30,001 to 40,000 lb (full report is registration-only; figure as reported, not checked by this project); https://truckingresearch.org/2026/07/analysis-of-the-operational-costs-of-trucking-2026-update/

Assumption: maintenance and tire cost per detour mile, dollars. Basis: ATRI, An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking, 2026 Update, reports repair and maintenance at $0.22 a mile in 2025, plus tires (full report is registration-only; figure as reported, not checked by this project); https://truckingresearch.org/2026/07/analysis-of-the-operational-costs-of-trucking-2026-update/
Assumption: a missed saving must beat this many dollars to count
